messages:
eli-cs: Ana from ParkLane reports sporadic 401s during SDK onboarding followed by short 429 spikes. She says this started after switching to very short-lived ephemeral tokens (TTL=6s) in mobile clients. Sample log: `auth=401 token=stale req=pl-42` then `gateway=429 req=pl-42 reason=burst_protect`
ana-customer: Yep. We refresh every 4s from our auth proxy and create a new SDK client in each background job. About 1 in 12 requests get 401 then a burst of 429s for ~8s.
ryan-eng: Two quick checks: are you reusing a client instance per process? and which region are devices hitting? Short TTL + new clients per job is a classic fanout.
ana-customer: We spin a client per job and region is hard-coded to eu-west.
ryan-eng: Root cause likely: tight TTL + synchronized refresh causes many near-simultaneous preflight/auth ops. A few tokens land as stale (401) then the gateway backpressures with 429 to protect the runtime. Also spawning new connections per job increases load.
infra-bot: log-extract queued: /logs/2324105678/pl-42 (attached)
ryan-eng: Log extract shows ~7 auth 401s then ~110 gateway 429s in a 12s window. Recommend: 1) increase ephemeral TTL to 30-60s; 2) switch to a single client instance per process (singleton) or use client pooling; 3) add randomized jitter to refresh schedules (0-3s); 4) honor Retry-After on 429s with exponential backoff; 5) avoid hard-coded region -> use 'auto' or shard clients per region.
mona-ops: We can add a temporary lenient burst window for ParkLane CIDR during the canary test. I'll create a 60m soft exemption rule and tag it for removal.
eli-cs: I'll schedule a 30-minute enablement call tomorrow 11:00 AM PT to watch metrics. Action items: eli-cs -> run call; ana -> roll canary (TTL & client reuse); ryan -> standby for logs; mona-ops -> apply soft exemption.
nana-customer: Thanks. We'll roll TTL=45s + single-client canary and add jitter. Will update here before the call.
ryan-eng: Small code sketch for mobile refresh jitter: ```js // pseudocode const jitter = Math.floor(Math.random()*3000); setTimeout(refreshToken, baseMs + jitter); // reuse a singleton client across jobs ```
eli-cs: Noted renewal risk reduced to "watching" if this stabilizes after the canary; we'll escalate to renewals if still flapping.
nana-customer: Appreciate the help — will report back by EOD.
